spawn.title: How thread::spawn works
spawn.description: Runs a closure on a new thread, at the same time as the rest of the program.

slides.caption: spawn starts a new thread and returns a JoinHandle immediately; it does not wait.
Meanwhile the new thread runs the closure and computes 2 + 2.
join() waits for it to finish and returns its result.
The closure must own what it uses: write move || ... to move variables into the thread.

join.title: How JoinHandle::join works
join.description: Waits for a thread to finish and returns what its closure returned.

slides.caption: join blocks until the thread is done, then gives back Ok(value), or Err if the thread panicked.
If you never join, the program may exit before the thread finishes its work.

sleep.title: How thread::sleep works
sleep.description: Pauses the current thread for at least the given time.

slides.caption: The thread stops; other threads keep running.
The OS wakes it after 50 ms or a bit more.
Never use sleep to wait for another thread: use join, a channel or a Condvar.

note.text: result: slept at least 50 ms: true

scope.title: How thread::scope works
scope.description: Starts threads that may borrow local variables; all of them finish before scope returns.

slides.caption: Because the threads are joined at the end of scope, they can safely borrow data.
Thread 2 sums [3, 4], at the same time.
The easiest way to split work over threads.

current.title: How thread::current works
current.description: A handle to the thread that is running this code.

slides.caption: Threads can have names, which show up in panic messages.
The main thread is called "main"; unnamed threads give None.

builder_spawn.title: How thread::Builder::spawn works
builder_spawn.description: Starts a thread with settings such as a name or a stack size.

slides.caption: Unlike thread::spawn, this returns a Result: creating a thread can fail.
A bigger stack helps deeply recursive code.

is_finished.title: How JoinHandle::is_finished works
is_finished.description: Checks whether the thread is done, without waiting.

slides.caption: is_finished never blocks; join() still has to be called to get the result.
Useful for showing progress while background work runs.

yield_now.title: How thread::yield_now works
yield_now.description: Lets the OS run other threads before this one continues.

slides.caption: It gives up the rest of this thread's time slice; it does not sleep for a fixed time.
The scheduler may run another thread.
Better options for waiting: join, channels, Condvar or park.

with.title: How LocalKey::with works
with.description: Gives a closure access to this thread's own copy of a thread_local! value.

slides.caption: Each thread sees its own value, starting from the initial one.
The other thread has a separate copy: also 1.
Declared with thread_local! { static COUNTER: Cell<u32> = Cell::new(0); }.

try_with.title: How LocalKey::try_with works
try_with.description: Like with, but returns an error instead of panicking if the value is already destroyed.

slides.caption: Only fails while the thread is shutting down and destructors run.

get.title: How LocalKey<Cell<T>>::get works
get.description: Reads a thread-local Cell value directly.

slides.caption: Only for Copy values in a Cell.

set.title: How LocalKey::set works
set.description: Replaces this thread's value of a thread-local Cell or RefCell.

slides.caption: Only the current thread's copy changes.

take.title: How LocalKey::take works
take.description: Takes this thread's value out, leaving the default.

slides.caption: Works for thread-local Cells and RefCells of Default types.
replace swaps in a value of your choice.

replace.title: How LocalKey::replace works
replace.description: Puts in a new value and returns the old one.

with_borrow.title: How LocalKey<RefCell<T>>::with_borrow works
with_borrow.description: Reads a thread-local RefCell inside a closure.

with_borrow_mut.title: How LocalKey<RefCell<T>>::with_borrow_mut works
with_borrow_mut.description: Changes a thread-local RefCell inside a closure.

slides.caption: A per-thread log or cache without locks.
Each thread keeps its own log.

available_parallelism.title: How thread::available_parallelism works
available_parallelism.description: An estimate of how many threads can run at the same time.

slides.caption: Usually the number of CPU cores available to the program.
It can fail in unusual environments, so it returns a Result.

park.title: How thread::park works
park.description: Puts the current thread to sleep until another thread unparks it.

slides.caption: park can also wake up spuriously, so check a condition in a loop.
Higher-level tools (channels, Condvar) are usually easier.

park_timeout.title: How thread::park_timeout works
park_timeout.description: Sleeps until unparked or until the time runs out.

slides.caption: Returns either way; it does not tell you which happened.
Measure the time yourself if you need to know.

panicking.title: How thread::panicking works
panicking.description: true while the current thread is unwinding from a panic.

slides.caption: Lets destructors behave differently during a panic.
A Drop running because of a panic: true.
Never panic again inside Drop when this is true.

id.title: How Thread::id works
id.description: A unique identifier for a thread.

slides.caption: Every thread gets its own ThreadId.
Useful as a key in per-thread statistics.

name.title: How Thread::name works
name.description: The thread's name, if it has one.

slides.caption: The main thread is called "main"; others only if named with Builder.

unpark.title: How Thread::unpark works
unpark.description: Wakes a parked thread (or makes its next park return at once).

slides.caption: If the thread is not parked yet, the wake-up is remembered.
The next park consumes it and returns.
Only one token is kept: several unparks count as one.

new.title: How thread::Builder::new works
new.description: Starts configuring a thread before spawning it.

slides.caption: Name and stack size can be set before starting.
spawn returns io::Result because creating a thread can fail.

builder-name.title: How thread::Builder::name works
builder-name.description: Gives the new thread a name.

slides.caption: Names appear in panic messages and debuggers.
Names must not contain a NUL byte.

stack_size.title: How thread::Builder::stack_size works
stack_size.description: Sets the stack size of the new thread in bytes.

slides.caption: The default stack is a few MB; deep recursion may need more.
The OS may round the size up.

spawn_scoped.title: How thread::Builder::spawn_scoped works
spawn_scoped.description: Starts a configured thread inside a scope, so it may borrow local data.

slides.caption: Combines Builder settings with thread::scope borrowing.

scope-spawn.title: How Scope::spawn works
scope-spawn.description: Starts a thread that may borrow from the enclosing scope.

slides.caption: All scoped threads finish before thread::scope returns.
Mutably borrowed data can be used by one thread at a time.

scoped_join_handle-join.title: How ScopedJoinHandle::join works
scoped_join_handle-join.description: Waits for a scoped thread and returns its result.

slides.caption: Without join, the scope still waits, but the result is lost.

scoped_join_handle-is_finished.title: How ScopedJoinHandle::is_finished works
scoped_join_handle-is_finished.description: Checks whether a scoped thread is done, without waiting.

thread.title: How ScopedJoinHandle::thread works
thread.description: The Thread handle of a scoped thread.

slides.caption: Use it to unpark the thread or read its name and id.

join_handle-thread.title: How JoinHandle::thread works
join_handle-thread.description: The Thread handle of a spawned thread.

slides.caption: Lets you unpark it or read its id while it runs.
Its id matches what the thread sees.

spawn_unchecked.title: How Builder::spawn_unchecked works
spawn_unchecked.description: Spawns a thread whose closure may borrow non-'static data (unsafe).

note.text: you guarantee the borrow outlives the thread

slides.caption: Join before the borrowed data goes away.
